chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked him about a man who is making up for Ramadan, is it permissible for him to break his fast after dawn but before midday if it becomes apparent to him? He said: 'If he intended that from the night, and it is from making up for Ramadan, then he should not break his fast and he should complete his fast.'

He said: And I asked him about a man who becomes apparent to him after dawn and the day rises, that he should fast that day and make it up from Ramadan, even if he did not intend that from the night. He said: 'Yes, he should fast it and count it, provided he does not do anything [that breaks the fast/intent].'

key_terms.قَضَاءِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up missed fasts of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up a missed Ramadan fast if one breaks it after dawn but before midday?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of intention (niyyah) for making up missed Ramadan fasts, distinguishing between those who pre-intended the fast from the night before, who must complete it, and those who decide to fast during the day, who may still count it as valid Qada provided no invalidating factor occurs. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that for Qada fasts, the strict requirement of nocturnal intention is relaxed compared to obligatory daily fasts, emphasizing the validity of the act even with late intention. This ruling underscores the practical ease granted to believers in fulfilling religious obligations, reflecting the broader Shia principle of facilitating worship without undue hardship.
